compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL's UPDATE statement uses FOR UPDATE locking semantics by default during the update operation. SQL Server's UPDATE may have different lock escalation and duration characteristics. If precise locking control is needed, consider adding explicit SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before the UPDATE statement

PostgreSQL procedures (PROCEDURE) can control transactions with COMMIT/ROLLBACK. If called within an existing transaction, the procedure participates in that transaction. SQL Server's behavior is similar, but verify transaction isolation level requirements
PostgreSQL procedures do not return row count messages to clients by default, making SET NOCOUNT ON unnecessary. This is a behavioral match
No error handling present in source procedure. Both SQL Server and PostgreSQL will raise errors on constraint violations or other issues. Consider adding explicit error handling if needed
